title: Put both AirPods Pro back in their case, each stem-first into its own well, and push the lid shut so its magnet holds it
instruction: Put both earbuds back in their charging case and close the lid.
context: Most people with wireless earbuds put them back in their case every time they take them out: 59 percent of Americans aged 12 and over own Bluetooth wireless headphones (Edison Research, 2025), and Apple's own steps are "Put your AirPods in their case. Close the lid.", as the buds "charge whenever they're in the case with the lid closed" and a charge lasts up to 6 hours of listening. The two wells are mirror images, so each bud goes only into its own side's well, stem first and the right way round: its 5.7 mm stem has to go down the well's narrow bore before the well's magnet pulls it home. A bud in the wrong well, or let go before its stem is down the bore, sits proud, and the lid then rests open on it instead of snapping shut. The case is 50.8 g and 21.7 mm deep, and a push on its open lid tips it, so the other hand holds it while the lid is pushed shut. Each 5.3 g bud lies on its side and has to be turned stem-down first. Here an AirPods Pro 2 case stands open, both buds beside it.
setup: Centimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the bench top. An Apple AirPods Pro 2 MagSafe Charging Case (Apple: 45.2 x 60.6 x 21.7 mm, 50.8 g) stands upright on the bench centred at (34, 2), its 60.6 mm width along y, its lid hinged along its far (+x) top edge and open at 115 degrees (Apple's drawing), leaning back away from the robot. Its top holds two wells, centred 17 mm either side of the case's centre, the left bud's at +y and the right bud's at -y, so the seated heads stand about 12 mm apart. Each well is a bore shaped to the bud's stem (5.7 x 7.6 mm, 23.3 mm long) with 0.75 to 0.8 mm of play a side and a chamfered mouth (2.5 mm a side, 4 mm deep), plus two key slots over its top: one for the rib on the stem's outer side (standing 2.2 mm off the stem) and one for the bump on its front. So each bud goes only into its own well, stem first, front toward the robot; in the other well its rib meets solid wall with the bud still 6 mm or more proud. A seated bud's head rests on the rim, 7.6 mm proud of it, and the shut lid clears it by 1.4 mm. Each well's magnet pulls a bud whose seat is within 7 mm of home toward the seat with 0.4 N, and not from farther away; the lid's magnet pulls it shut over its last 5 degrees and holds it with 1 N at its edge. The two AirPods Pro 2 earbuds (Apple: 30.9 x 21.8 x 24.0 mm, 5.3 g each; bud head 17.3 mm deep: Apple's 24.0 mm includes the silicone ear tip, which squashes in the real case and is not modelled) lie on their sides on the bench, stem toward the robot (-x), front up: the left one at (26, 14) and the right one at (26, 22). Frictions: case on bench 0.4, buds 0.5. Well, bore, key, magnet, hinge and friction figures are estimates from maker photos (Apple publishes none). The case may be held or lifted, as long as it never tips past 20 degrees; where it ends counts. Nothing else is on the bench. Both arms start at their ready pose, grippers open; in the demo the right hand holds the case and the left seats both buds and shuts the lid, but either hand may do either. Reset: buds back on their marks, front up; lid open at 115 degrees.
scoring: Terms. Judged means the state at the end, once both grippers have been at least 3 cm from the case and everything still for 1 s (real trial: from the trial video); before that nothing is judged (0). Partial credit is recomputed from the current state at every step and nothing is carried over from an earlier moment, so a bud taken out, a case moved or a hand back at the case changes the score at once. A bud is seated when it is in its own well within 0.5 mm of fully home, 1 mm of its axis in each direction, 5 degrees of upright and 10 degrees of its turn (real trial: turn the open case upside down and both buds stay in). The lid is shut when it is closed within 1 degree (real trial: turn the closed case upside down and the lid stays shut). Tiers: each bud seated in its own well: 0.25; lid shut over both seated buds: 0.5 more. The case must end upright within 5 degrees and within 3 cm of where it stood, else 0 (real trial: it stands on its base inside a tape outline drawn 3 cm outside its footprint). Zeros that stick: a case tipped past 20 degrees at any moment, or a bud off the bench. Free: which bud goes first, which hand does what, and lifting or holding the case cost nothing by themselves. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. The run ends with success once 1.0 has held for 1 s.
run_limit: 3,000 steps (150 s at 20 Hz), about 2.6 times the 58 s demo
reset_notes: Nothing is random: the case at its mark with the lid open at 115 degrees, both buds on their marks lying on their sides, front up. In a real trial, photograph the buds on their marks once and match that photo at each reset; about 20 seconds (estimate), nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. Case and buds at Apple's published sizes and masses, except the bud head, 17.3 mm deep (real 24.0 mm with its silicone ear tip): the tip squashes in the real case and is not modelled. Wells, keys, hinge and frictions: estimates from maker photos. Each well's magnet is code: a 0.4 N pull toward its seat within 7 mm of it, the case taking the reaction. The lid's magnet is a drive in its hinge: 1 N at its edge over the last 5 degrees. The demo reads object poses and the lid's angle.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0 (one valid run: 3,000 steps, one session, none lost); demo: 1.0 (both hands, 1,163 steps); the tested one-hand run: 0.0 (its lid push tips the case); buds swapped: 0.0; one bud left on the bench: 0.25; a seated bud pulled out after both were in: 0.25; case pushed 6 cm after seating: 0.
